focus: The new Command.GizmoOnGUIShrunk prefix/postfix and the refactor of the GizmoOnGUI patch into shared RightClick/Badge helpers.
diffSource: since the oldest restore point still kept (2026-10-21T20:45:34Z); older ones were pruned, so the chat's first changes may be missing

findings.title: Autocast badge draws over the gizmo's hotkey label
findings.detail: Command.GizmoOnGUIInt prints the hotkey at the button's top-left (x+5,y+3 full; x+3,y+0 shrunk). Badge() draws an opaque TexUI.GrayTextBG box at topLeft+(3,2) after the original runs (postfix), covering it. Command_Ability copies ability.def.hotKey, and nine Ideology AbilityDefs (plus mod abilities, e.g. Alpha Mechs) set Misc12, so on those gizmos turning autocast on hides the cast key. Move the badge in Patch_CommandAbility_Autocast.Badge to the bottom-left, or offset it by Text.LineHeight when command.hotKey != null.

findings.title: Shrunk patch is needed and does not double up with the GizmoOnGUI patch
findings.detail: Command.GizmoOnGUIShrunk calls GizmoOnGUIInt directly and never reaches virtual GizmoOnGUI, so a shrunk Command_Ability goes through only the shrunk patch and a full-size one only the Command_Ability.GizmoOnGUI patch: no double badge or double right-click handling. No vanilla or corpus class overrides GizmoOnGUIShrunk, so patching the base reaches every vanilla Command_Ability subclass. The parameter names (topLeft, size; topLeft, maxWidth) match the originals.

findings.title: VEF/VPE ability gizmos are a different Command_Ability and never get the menu
findings.detail: VPE's Command_Ability_Psycast derives from VEF.Abilities.Command_Ability, not RimWorld.Command_Ability, so the `is Command_Ability` check never matches it and those gizmos get no autocast menu or badge. The opening comment, which names VEF's autocast toggle, could be read as covering them.

findings.title: WouldAffect reads PsychicSensitivity from a 250-tick cache where vanilla reads it fresh
findings.detail: Psycast.CanApplyPsycastTo calls GetStatValue(StatDefOf.PsychicSensitivity) uncached. WouldAffect uses cacheStaleAfterTicks 250, so for up to about 4 s a pawn whose sensitivity just dropped to 0 can still count toward an AoE centre. It is harmless as long as the driver's final AbilityAIDriver.Valid -> verb.ValidateTarget path repeats the vanilla psycast check. It only affects scoring, and the code comment already says this was a deliberate trade.

findings.title: Cover's SpawnedNear counts a spawned thing of any faction
findings.detail: listerThings.ThingsOfDef(spawns) is not filtered by faction or who spawned it, so any skipshield within the radius stops the caster from casting its own, including an enemy's. This is my opinion of the intent, not a defect the corpus shows.

checked: all four patches in AbilityAIAutocast.cs bind (verify_patches: 4 of 4 resolved)

the prefix's rect for GizmoOnGUI matches vanilla's (GetWidth(maxWidth) x 75f); the shrunk rect matches GizmoOnGUIShrunk's (size x size, GetShrunkSize = 36f)
GizmoGridDrawer calls GizmoOnGUIShrunk only for shrinkableCommands, and Command_Ability sets shrinkable = true, so the shrunk path is reached for abilities
no subclass in vanilla or the corpus overrides GizmoOnGUIShrunk, so the base-class patch reaches all vanilla Command_Ability subclasses
Command_Ability.Ability is a public property; null ability and null pawn are guarded before use

every Keyed string used (AAI_Mode_*, AAI_Badge_*) exists in Languages/English/Keyed/AbilityAI.xml
